q: 75. Free float is the
explain: Free float is defined as the amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the earliest start time of any succeeding activities. It is a portion of the total float that remains positive.

q: 76. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to the critical path is known as
explain: The path with the second-lowest amount of float (next to the critical path, which has zero float) is technically referred to in this context as the semi-critical path.

q: 77. In CPM
options: time optimization is given prime importance
cost optimization is given prime importance
cost is directly proportional to time
explain: Unlike PERT (which is probabilistic and time-oriented), CPM is deterministic and focuses heavily on the trade-off between time and cost, prioritizing cost optimization.

q: 78. Which method is known as minimum cost or maximum time schedule method
explain: CPM (Critical Path Method) is designed to find the schedule that minimizes total project cost by balancing direct and indirect costs over time.

q: 79. Critical path
explain: The critical path is the longest path through the network; therefore, it contains the activities with the least amount of flexibility or 'minimum slack' (usually zero).

q: 80. Critical path is
explain: By definition, the critical path is the sequence of activities that takes the longest time to complete, determining the shortest possible project duration.

q: 81. For completion of a project, the CPM of the network represents
explain: The Critical Path Method identifies the minimum time required to complete the entire project based on the sequence of dependent tasks.

q: 82. The time below witch the duration can not be further reduced is known as
explain: Crash time is the absolute minimum time in which an activity can be completed by employing additional resources, regardless of cost.

q: 83. The cost corresponding to crash time is
explain: Crashing involves increasing resources to save time, which maximizes direct costs. Because the duration is shortest, indirect costs are minimized, but the total cost often peaks.

q: 84. The cost corresponding to the completion of activity within normal time is
explain: Normal cost is the expenditure associated with completing an activity in its 'normal time' using standard resources and methods.

q: 85. The direct cost of a project with respect to normal time is
explain: In the time-cost relationship, direct cost is at its lowest (minimum) when the project is executed at a normal, non-accelerated pace.

q: 86. The reduction in project time normally results in
options: decreasing the direct cost and increasing indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and decreasing the indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
decreasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
explain: Reducing time (crashing) requires more labor/equipment (increasing direct cost) but reduces the time-dependent overheads like rent or utilities (decreasing indirect cost).

q: 87. The total cost verses time curve of an activity is
explain: The total cost curve is generally represented as a parabola or U-shaped because it is the summation of a decreasing indirect cost and an increasing direct cost curve.

q: 88. Assuming that the cost varies with time, the cost – slope is defined as
options: (crash cost - normal cost) / (normal time - crash time)
explain: Cost slope represents the increase in cost per unit of time saved. It is calculated as the change in cost divided by the change in time.

q: 89. Direct cost of a project is due to
options: establishment charges as salaries to administrative staff
cost of materials and wages of labor
explain: Direct costs are those that can be attributed directly to a specific activity, such as the physical materials used and the wages of the workers performing the task.

q: 90. Indirect cost of the project
options: decreases up to optimum duration and then increase with duration
explain: Indirect costs are time-dependent expenses (overheads); the longer the project lasts, the more these costs accumulate.

q: 91. Total project cost
options: initially reduces with time and then increases with further increases
explain: Total cost is the sum of direct and indirect costs. It typically decreases as duration increases toward the 'optimum' point, then starts to rise again as indirect costs dominate.

q: 92. The reduction in project time normally results in
options: decreasing the direct cost and increasing indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and decreasing the indirect cost
increasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
decreasing the direct cost and indirect cost both
explain: As previously noted, reducing project time involves crashing (higher direct costs) while saving on time-based overheads (lower indirect costs).

q: 93. In a time-cost optimization using CPM the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: To reduce project duration most economically, we crash the critical activity that has the lowest cost slope (cheapest to crash first).

q: 94. The amount of time required performing any event in case of PERT should be ................... CPM.
explain: Because PERT deals with uncertain/probabilistic time estimates and CPM uses deterministic ones, the actual time required can vary based on the nature of the project.

q: 95. PERT technique of network analysis is useful for
explain: PERT is ideally suited for Research and Development projects where the duration of activities is uncertain and has not been performed before.

q: 96. An event is
options: a definite position of an activity
explain: An event represents a point in time (the start or end of an activity) and does not consume time or resources itself; it marks the terminals.

q: 97. PERT means
options: pertinent programming related to a project
explain: PERT is the standard acronym for Program Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 98. PERT is
explain: PERT focuses on milestones or 'events' (reaching a specific stage), whereas CPM focuses on the 'activities' or tasks themselves.

q: 99. 'Wait' in PERT, belongs to the category of
explain: In the context of network analysis, waiting is considered a 'dummy activity' or an activity because it consumes time, even if it doesn't consume physical resources.

q: 100. In PERT technique, completion of an activity is called
explain: The event at the end (arrowhead) of an activity is known as the head event, signifying the completion of that activity.

q: 101. The time corresponding to minimum total project cost is
explain: In time-cost optimization, the 'optimum duration' (which minimizes total cost) usually falls between the crash time and normal time, often aligning with the optimistic perspective of cost-efficiency.

q: 102. The time with which direct cost does not reduce with the increase in time is known as
explain: Normal time is the duration beyond which increasing time further does not lead to any further reduction in direct costs.

q: 103. The benefit of the PERT network is taken by the management in
options: readjusting the time to meet the target
explain: PERT provides a comprehensive framework for scheduling, inter-departmental coordination, and dynamic readjustment based on probability.

q: 104. Which of the following time estimate is related to PERT?
explain: PERT uses a 'three-time estimate' approach (Optimistic, Pessimistic, and Most Likely) to account for uncertainty.

q: 105. The event which act as head as well as tail for different activities is, called
explain: An internal node in a network that marks the finish of one activity and the start of another is a dual role event.

q: 106. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day, pessimistic time is 11 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Using the PERT formula $t_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p) / 6$: $(1 + 4(3) + 11) / 6 = 24 / 6 = 4$ days.

q: 107. Of the following, the PERT event is
explain: Events are instantaneous milestones. 'Concrete cured' signifies a finished state (event), whereas the others are ongoing processes (activities).

q: 108. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT analysis relies on all three time estimates to calculate the expected mean time.

q: 109. In PERT analysis, the start and end of event is represented by
explain: Events are graphically represented as circles or rectangles, commonly referred to as nodes in a network diagram.

q: 110. The probability of completion of any activity within its expected time in PERT is
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) in a normal distribution represents the 50% probability mark (the mean).

q: 111. If the probability factor is zero, the chances of completing the project in scheduled time are
explain: A probability factor (Z-score) of zero means the scheduled time equals the expected time, resulting in a 50% chance of success.

q: 112. You are going to design a new computer programme, which would you like to prefer?
explain: Software development involves high uncertainty in task durations, making the probabilistic PERT method more suitable than deterministic CPM.

q: 113. Bar chart is used for minor project, CPM is used for repetitive work while PERT is used for
options: limited time and unlimited resources types of work
uncertainty time and resources types of work
explain: PERT is specifically designed for non-repetitive projects where time and resource requirements are uncertain.

q: 114. Standard deviation when the optimistic time is 1 day, pessimistic time is 11 days and most likely time is 3 days
explain: Standard deviation ($\sigma$) = $(t_p - t_o) / 6$. Here, $(11 - 1) / 6 = 10 / 6 = 1.67$ days.

q: 115. In PERT analysis the actual performance of task is known as
explain: The actual work or performance required to progress from one event to another is termed an activity.

q: 116. Line of balance technique is used for
options: comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: Line of Balance (LOB) is a management control process used for highly repetitive projects to compare actual progress against the plan.

q: 117. In PERT, optimistic time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Optimistic time ($t_o$) assumes everything goes perfectly, representing the minimum possible duration.

q: 118. In PERT, pessimistic time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Pessimistic time ($t_p$) assumes everything goes wrong (excluding major disasters), representing the maximum duration.

q: 119. In PERT, the most likely time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: The most likely time ($t_m$) is the duration that would occur most frequently if the activity were repeated many times.

q: 120. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is equal to
explain: The weighted average (expected time) in PERT is calculated using the formula $(a + 4m + b) / 6$.

q: 121. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: Individual activity durations in PERT are assumed to follow a Beta distribution.

q: 122. Negative slack occurs
options: when latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule, often caused by resource shortages or delays.

q: 123. A stage or point where all previous jobs merging in it are completed and all further jobs bursting out are still to be completed is known as a
explain: This describes a node in the network, which is technically an event.

q: 124. The latest allowable time for any event i is equal to
explain: To ensure no following activities are delayed, the latest allowable time is the minimum of the late finishes of succeeding activities minus their durations.

q: 125. SLACK time refers to an
explain: Slack is specifically associated with events (the difference between $T_L$ and $T_E$), while 'float' is associated with activities.

q: 126. The minimum number of years required to complete any research project may be
explain: Research projects have variable timelines depending on complexity and findings.

q: 127. An event is indicated on the network by a number enclosed in
explain: While circles are standard, various shapes like squares or ellipses can be used to represent nodes in different conventions.

q: 128. Slack time in PERT analysis
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: Critical events are those on the path with the least amount of slack (zero or negative).

q: 129. The area under the beta-curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) is the mean of the distribution, which bisects the area under the probability curve.

q: 130. For a beta-distribution curve, if t0 is the optimistic time and tp the pessimistic time then the standard deviation will be equal to
explain: The standard deviation is defined as one-sixth of the range between pessimistic and optimistic times.

q: 131. For a curve, larger the variance
explain: Variance is a measure of spread; a higher variance means the actual time could deviate significantly from the mean, increasing uncertainty.

q: 132. If an activity has its optimistic, most likely and pessimistic time are 2, 4 & 6 respectively, then its expected time and variance are respectively
133. tij and tEij indicates the time required for completion of an activity in CPM and PERT respectively. Here the subscript E stands for
explain: The 'E' in $t_E$ stands for 'Expected' time, which incorporates the uncertainty inherent in PERT.

q: 134. Which of the following does not represent an activity?
options: the office area is being cleaned
explain: 'Site located' is a completed state or milestone (event), not a process that consumes time.

q: 135. In a CPM/PERT network, the number of event is
options: more than the number of activity
equal to the number of activity
explain: The relationship between the number of events and activities depends entirely on the network topology and the use of dummy activities.

q: 136. The technique used for the management and development of Polaris Missile in American Navy Force is
explain: PERT was famously developed by the US Navy in the late 1950s specifically for the Polaris missile project.

q: 137. Positive slack indicates
explain: Positive slack means there is extra time available, implying the project or event is ahead of its required deadline.

q: 138. Negative slack indicates
explain: Negative slack means the earliest expected time is later than the latest allowable time, indicating a delay.

q: 139. The slack for an event i is given by
explain: Slack for an event is calculated as the Latest Allowable occurrence time ($T_L$) minus the Earliest Expected occurrence time ($T_E$).

q: 140. Variance is
options: Sum of time duration / number of jobs
difference between time and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviation
explain: Mathematically, variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean.

q: 141. The square root of the variance is known as
explain: By definition, the standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

q: 142. The variance will be zero if
explain: Variance is only zero if all data points (durations) are exactly equal to the mean.

q: 143. The chart which gives an estimate about the amount of materials handling between various work stations is known as :
explain: A travel chart is used to analyze the movement of materials and personnel between different locations.

q: 144. One of the tools for monitoring and evaluation of projects is :
explain: The Logical Framework Approach (LFA) is a standard methodology for planning and evaluating project progress.

q: 145. Crashing is
explain: Crashing is the process of shortening the duration of project activities by adding resources.

q: 146. Economic saving of time is obtained by crashing
explain: Crashing the critical activity with the lowest cost slope provides the most cost-effective time reduction.

q: 147. Crash project duration is obtained by adding the
options: crash durations for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities along the critical path
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path
explain: The total crashed duration is the sum of the crash times of all activities forming the critical path.

q: 148. At an event other than final event if no activity emerges it results in an error called
explain: Dangling occurs when an activity is disconnected from the network flow, ending at a node that isn't the final project event.

q: 149. Earned value analysis is used for comparing----------- of the project
explain: Earned Value Management (EVM) measures project performance by comparing actual work done against the baseline plan.

q: 150. A frequency distribution curve
options: having single lump is called unimodal curve
if symmetrical is called normal curve
if unsymmetrical is called skew curve
explain: These are standard statistical terms describing the shape and symmetry of frequency distributions.
